summary: The study describes a method to enhance atomic-layer deposition (ALD) of tungsten nitride (W–N) diffusion barriers for Cu interconnects. The process uses WF6 and NH3 as precursors, with NH3 pulse plasma introduced during the ALD cycle to modify the surface and prevent catalytic reactions. The W–N films are deposited at 350 °C with a deposition rate of 2.2 Å/cycle. The films show uniform N concentration and good thermal stability, preventing Cu diffusion after annealing at 700 °C for 30 minutes.
evidence: We have suggested an atomic layer deposition (ALD) method for preparing W–N films on Si and non-Si surfaces by using WF6 and NH3. In this method, during the ALD cycle we have introduced NH3 gas with pulse rf power, resulting in a NH3 pulse plasma that modified Si and SiO2 surfaces to become Si–N and Si–O–N surfaces. With this method, we can obtain a uniformly distributed N concentration in the W–N films deposited on the Si and non-Si surfaces with the deposition rate of ~2.2 Å/cycle at 350 °C. As a diffusion barrier for the Cu interconnect, high-resolution transmission electronic microscopy reveals that after annealing at 700 °C for 30 min, 22 nm thick W–N successfully prevents Cu diffusion.
